redistribution_classes.meaning: AGID-created metadata and non-geographic fixtures only.
Open G-NAF or ABS material with attribution, source-specific conditions and mailing-purpose restrictions preserved.
Australia Post PAF or postcode product material available only under the applicable contract; no row or geometry is public by default.
Geoscape Buildings and address-link artifacts remain product- and customer-rights partitioned.
Permitted live validation evidence may be retained only to the extent allowed by its product terms and purpose.

sources.production_scope: Pinned licensed postcode-data release or permitted lookup receipt, segregated by contract and publication rights.
sources.terms_note: Australia Post identifies its postcode list as the current complete reference; the free list is non-commercial and commercial use requires a licence.

sources.production_scope: Pinned monthly licensed PAF snapshot or permitted verification receipt within approved use and retention terms.
sources.terms_note: PAF is updated monthly from Australia Post ATLAS data and includes physical and postal delivery records. Contract rights govern access, storage and redistribution.

sources.provider: Geoscape Australia for the Australian Government
sources.production_scope: Pinned G-NAF release with GDA94/GDA2020 projection, EULA, attribution, privacy and external-territory partition recorded.
sources.terms_note: G-NAF is open address data, but its EULA prohibits using it to compile addresses for sending mail unless each address is verified by a secondary source as capable of receiving mail. G-NAF postcode values are commonly locality-derived rather than address-level Australia Post assignment.

sources.production_scope: Pinned ASGS Postal Areas edition with boundary vintage, Mesh Block base, exclusions and attribution recorded; Edition 3 remains the production POA source until Edition 4 POA is published and qualified.
sources.terms_note: POAs approximate postcodes by allocating Mesh Blocks. They are not authoritative Australia Post boundaries and exclude non-street-delivery codes such as PO boxes, mailback, large receivers and specialist codes.

sources.production_scope: Pinned licensed Buildings release and permitted building_address relationship artifact, segregated from open G-NAF and public outputs by product rights.
sources.terms_note: The Buildings product supplies building geometry and a building_address relation between building PID and address PID/address-detail PID with relationship confidence. Product licensing and field rights remain separate from G-NAF.

sources.production_scope: Pinned ASGS edition and boundary release used only for administrative and statistical context.
sources.terms_note: ASGS boundaries supply statistical context and cannot create, clip or replace Australia Post postcode assignments.

artifact_partitions.rule: PAF and commercial postcode rows stay outside public Git and public caches unless explicit contract rights permit a named artifact.
G-NAF retains release, EULA, attribution, geocode method, lifecycle and secondary-mail-verification status.
POA geometry retains ASGS edition and noncanonical official-derived classification; excluded delivery categories are never filled by inference.
Building geometry and building_address relations retain product rights and are not silently copied into the open G-NAF partition.
Administrative and statistical boundaries retain geography level and edition and never inherit postal authority.
CX, CC and NF are partitioned to their ISO country packs before all AU artifacts and indexes are built.
Recipients, residents, owners, customer IDs, change-of-address records, parcel-locker customer numbers and delivery instructions never enter public artifacts.
Non-geographic fixtures only; never promotion evidence.
